title: Ingest Edge Agent Contract and Rate Control Guidance
summary: Operational guidance and interface contract for lightweight edge ingest agents that forward control evidence to central collection infrastructure. Focus areas: deterministic headers for audit correlation, per-tenant rate-control tokens, graceful backpressure/queueing modes, and minimal sink compatibility shims for SIEM and log stacks.
goals: 1) Define a compact, stable contract for agents running in customer-managed or colocated environments so evidence is auditable end-to-end. 2) Provide optional on-agent controls to avoid bursting upstream (protecting our SIEM and Kafka clusters). 3) Standardize sampling and TTL semantics so downstream retention/archival policies can be automated. 4) Document migration guidance from current collector implementations to the new tokenized-rate model.
design_overview: Background: Multiple teams run lightweight collectors at region edges or in private deployments. We have observed bursts that cause backfills and delayed evidence ingestion. This spec introduces a small, low-latency token scheme combined with a per-tenant leaky-bucket rate limiter, a deterministic audit header set, and a sink-compatibility layer that emits both native and normalized forms.
agent_contract: Message envelope: each outgoing event MUST include the following HTTP headers or equivalent envelope fields: X-RW-Evidence-ID (uuid v4), X-RW-Timestamp (ISO8601 UTC), X-RW-Tenant (tenant-id), X-RW-Source-Host (agent fqdn or id), X-RW-Trace (optional trace id). Body shape: either (a) native payload (original JSON from source) plus metadata block, or (b) normalized audit object with fields: action, subject, resource, outcome, before/after snapshots (if available). Schema versions must use X-RW-Schema-Version header. Contract for authentication: agents use scoped short-lived certs (mTLS) or signed tokens; tokens must include scope claim indicating permitted tenants and an Ingest-Rate attribute used by token exchanges.
backpressure_and_rate_control: Two complementary mechanisms: 1) Tokenized allowance: the control-plane issues time-limited "rate tokens" (JWT-like) that embed allowed qps and burst budget. Agents request a token refresh periodically and include the token in the X-RW-Rate-Token header. If token is missing or expired, upstream accepts at best-effort with lower priority. 2) Local leaky-bucket: the agent enforces a per-tenant bucket with configurable capacity and drain rate. When bucket is full the agent switches modes: (fast-path) drop non-essential telemetry with a local sampled-synthetic event logged, (safe-queue) persist to local disk with FIFO eviction policy, or (apply-backoff) slow read/poll loops for the source to reduce incoming rate. Recommendations: default capacity 500 events, drain 50 events/sec; for private deployments default to 5x to account for network variance. Metrics exported: agent.rate.allowed, agent.rate.used, agent.queue.depth, agent.drop.count, agent.token.expiry.
sampling_and_retention: Sampling gates: agents should support conditional sampling rules evaluated on metadata (tenant, action, resource) with an ordered rule list. Each rule defines keep/p95 target and deterministic hashing salt to allow consistent sampling across restarts. Retention TTL semantics: evidence items MUST carry retention_hint (short|standard|extended) mapped to retention windows in the control plane. Default mapping: short=7d, standard=90d, extended=365d. Sampling for high-volume actions: recommend deterministic 1-in-N where N is chosen to keep event cardinality within cluster budgets. Agents must emit sampling.decided boolean and sampling.seed to allow downstream reconstructions. Archival markers: a separate marker event indicating evidence moved to long-term archive must be emitted when archival completes.
sink_compatibility_and_transformations: To reduce coupling to downstream systems, agents include a sink compatibility shim: each event is emitted in two parallel channels from the agent (if configured): native_sink and normalized_sink. native_sink forwards the original producer format (for vendor-specific SIEM parsers), normalized_sink emits our canonical audit model. For Kafka sinks: topic naming convention rw.evidence.<tenant>.<env> and partitioning by X-RW-Evidence-ID hash. For syslog/CEF sinks: agents must translate normalized fields into CEF key/value pairs and append X-RW-Evidence-ID in the extension. For Elastic/Opensearch: include a dedicated rw_index_hint and a minimal mapping file shipped with agent releases. Transformation rules must be idempotent and declared in a local transforms.json so operators can inspect and adjust. Compatibility versions for transforms must be included with the X-RW-Transform-Version header.
rollout_and_migration_notes: Phased rollout: Start with passive mode where agent emits normalized_sink in addition to existing stream (no consumer changes). Phase 1: Deploy edge agents in a canary subset of customers (low traffic tenants) and monitor agent.queue.depth and drop.count. Phase 2: Enable rate tokens for canary tenants and enforce local leaky-bucket. Phase 3: Flip normalized_sink to be the primary ingestion path and route old streams to archival. Migration checklist items: update SIEM ingestion mappings, add rw_index_hint mappings, create retention policies matching retention_hint. Known risks: token expiration causing transient drops — mitigation: jittered refresh + grace window in token validation. Tooling: provide a troubleshooting CLI: rw-ingestctl dump-queue, rw-ingestctl token-refresh, rw-ingestctl transform-verify.
